question: Should free_tier.unit gain `records` for allowances counted in returned data rows or records?
why: Four records state a free tier counted in returned records or rows under another unit: crawler-scraper/brightdata (5,000 records a month, unit requests), crawler-scraper/octoparse (50,000 exported rows a month and 2,000 MCP records a week or a month, mixed), crawler-scraper/outscraper (returned businesses and reviews beside searches and pages, mixed) and data-apis/visual-crossing (1,000 weather records a day, mixed). The other records of the store whose free_tier.stated names records or rows count stored records (DNS records, search-index records) or rows read, and stay objects or requests. requests counts calls, so an allowance in returned records under it misstates what one call returns. Octoparse would move from mixed to records; Outscraper stays mixed because its searches and pages are requests. AGENTS.md section 2 rule 12 extends a vocabulary when a value fits no term; a rules session adds records (a row is a record) and moves brightdata and visual-crossing. Store commit 0398f4dc0405, fr sql over $.free_tier.stated and $.free_tier.unit.
